issues.description: Method calculateRemainingOrderNumber(): The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies calculateRemainingOrderNumber() with signature 'calculateRemainingOrderNumber(): int' — it should return an int representing the number of remaining orders. In the solution repository (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) the method is implemented as 'public void calculateRemainingOrderNumber()' and only prints order numbers instead of returning an int. This return-type mismatch between the specification and the provided implementation will confuse students about the correct method signature and may break tests or example usages that expect an int result.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and implementation consistent. Preferred fix: change the implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java to 'public int calculateRemainingOrderNumber()' and return the number of remaining orders (for example: 'return this.orders.length;'), optionally keeping any printing as a side-effect. Alternatively, if the intended behavior is to only print order numbers, update the problem statement/UML to declare the method as void and update tests and examples accordingly. Ensure tests and documentation are updated to reflect the chosen signature.
